title: Stallioneer Auth, inventory, and Options checkpoint
content:
Stallioneer had a larger consolidation pass after a few days away from it. The theme was less about adding a flashy new feature and more about deciding where each responsibility belongs: Auth owns accounts, Inventory owns daily catalog work, Bulk should stop duplicating Inventory, and Options should become the quiet place for local library management.

What changed:

  • Auth-first account model: Stallioneer moved further into central Auth. The existing catalog is assigned to wm, account-level inventory separation is now the direction, and the old Stallioneer-local account permissions section was removed because those controls belong in Auth.
  • Inventory and Bulk alignment: Inventory and Bulk now share more of the same visual and functional language: matching stat bars, matching book-table columns, compact copy icons, quick copied feedback, and less repeated page scaffolding.
  • Bulk is being folded back: import/export moved off Bulk and into Options, which keeps Bulk from becoming a second Inventory page with slightly different controls.
  • Options became the control surface: Tags, Collections, and Locations now live in compact dropdown panels on Options. Import is paused/commented for later, while CSV and PDF export remain available.
  • Export was simplified: Full Export appears first, Export PDF sits below it, and PDF field selection now uses blue active toggle pills instead of plain checkbox rows.
  • Shared styling tightened: the current top-banner page link now turns green across Stallioneer, preserving the normal hover behavior while making the active page easier to read.

This matters because Stallioneer is starting to behave less like a pile of catalog forms and more like a durable personal inventory app. The structure is clearer: Auth handles identity and permissions, Inventory remains the daily working surface, Options handles local library controls, and Bulk can be reduced into only the batch functions that still truly need to exist.
